newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish reindeer starved by thick snow.
newsitem.headline: Finnish reindeer starved by thick snow.

text.p: Exceptionally heavy snowfall in Lapland has brought some reindeer herds to the brink of starvation, Finnish experts said on Monday.

Reindeer calves have starved to death as exceptional fluctuations in temperature have covered the lichen they normally eat under an almost impenetrable layer of snow and ice, farming advisor Taisto Pohjanvesi told Reuters by telephone.
"This is a very severe crisis," he said, adding 10,000 of Finland's 210,000 reindeer may die.
Some farmers are buying extra fodder for the animals but the cost could prove prohibitive, with a reindeer carcass selling at $170-190 and the feed costing about $65 for this season alone, he said.
Reindeer can normally easily dig through the snow. But this year it has become so hard and thick it takes more energy to tunnel through than the plants can give the animals, he said.
